$comment: The Rite (design doc §7): each region's staged offering ritual and the Migration gate. Run 1 is authored here; runs 2+ come from the generator (Phase 4) using this as the template. A verse completes when chooseCount of its five slots are filled; slots are weighted so the spotlight crafts are the cheapest path. Resource offerings credit Renown at trade value; deed/specimen/fragment slots carry a fixed renownGrant, and so do resource slots offering unsellable MATERIALS (ingots, cordage — trade value is zero, the validator enforces the grant; values approximate amount x the material's notional input-derived worth). Verse lines live in dialogue.json (verses), verse sites in zones.json (verseSite). Quantities are first-pass — tune in Phase 3 against the §8 pacing targets.
$zoneRampNote: Goods amounts carry a GEOMETRIC zone ramp: x3.5 per zone order, anchored at zone 2 (zone 3 x3.5, 4 x12, 5 x43, 6 x150, 7 x525, 8 x1840, rounded clean). The zone-8 row was derived from zone 7's rather than re-spread from scratch: its two raw slots sit at zone 7's raw geometric mean x3.5 (35.5M each in Coin worth), and its craft slot at x3.0 of that mean, which is exactly the ratio felted-cloak carries at zone 7 (30.5M against a 10.1M raw mean) — so the valueSpread texture rides across the ramp step instead of being recomputed with a different pivot. The within-run power curve grows ~x2.5 per zone step — each later zone debuts against more stacked tool mults, more banked Verdure and more kith slots — so the ask outruns it by ~x1.4 per verse ON PURPOSE: at x2.5 the ramp merely held each debut verse level with the last (~20-40 min of its own node's production), and a Rite whose verses all cost the same is a Rite with no shape. At x3.5 each verse asks about half again as long as the one before, so verse 7 is the run's event and not its seventh errand. demandGrowth^m stacks on top as the fold-over-fold stretch. Zones 1-2 are pinned by the hour-one pacing targets (verse 1 ~30 min) — do not ramp them. Material-slot renownGrants scale WITH their amounts (grant ~ amount x notional worth, the no-tax promise); deed/specimen/sketch counts do NOT take this ramp — they price in taps and luck, not stock. The generator copies deed and sketch counts straight from this table and scales only their grants; specimen counts are no longer copied at all — the generator PRICES them off each verse's own goods asks, see generator.$specimenSlotNote, which supersedes $specimenRampNote below for every zone past order 2. Zones 4-7 never play from this table (fold-gated past run 1) — their rows exist as the generator's value anchors. Ramp is model-derived 2026-07-31, NOT playtested — the run-3-to-run-6 sitting judges it, and it pushes the full-map estimate out past the FTP ~9-12 d / paid ~4-6 d that the x2.5 pass was measured against.
$specimenRampNote: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-12 by generator.$specimenSlotNote, which prices the specimen slot off each verse's goods asks rather than tabling it — the linear-accrual premise this note rests on is not what Simulation.Deliver does. The counts below survive as the FLOOR, and still stand outright on zone order 1-2. Kept for the reasoning, not the numbers. Original note follows. Specimen slots carry their OWN ramp, x1.6 per zone order anchored at 1 on the river bend, rounded clean: 1 · 2 · 3 · 5 · 8 across zones 4-8 (zones 1-2 ask for a Decent and stay pinned at 1 with the rest of the hour-one table). Added 2026-08-03, because a flat count of 1 across every zone meant the slot stopped being an ask: the goods beside it ramp x3.5 a zone, so what was a fair quarter of the river bend's verse was ~1/1500th of the peaks' — a slot answered out of the drawer by any warden who had ever caught a windfall, and free of decision in a choose-3-of-5. It cannot take the goods ramp: Choice comes from a per-batch roll (design S5), so specimens accrue LINEARLY in posted familiars x time x choice chance while the goods economy compounds; x3.5 would ask 150 of them at the peaks against maybe 20 an hour, a wall no upgrade curve can move. x1.6 tracks roughly what the choice-chance stack is worth by each zone's point in a run (0.5% base plus Field Press, the plates, Verdant Eye, the Folio spreads) times the kith slots earned by then, so a deep specimen slot costs ~20-30 min of node time and the ask stays inside the verse's own pacing target. It is still the cheap slot at depth ON PURPOSE — the luck lane must not become the wall — and the Folio is competing for the same specimens, which is the tension the ramp is there to create. renownGrants scale WITH the counts (per-specimen worth unchanged: 1000 · 2500 · 4000 · 7000 · 10000) so a bigger ask is not also a quieter one; they stay small against the goods slots by design, because a slot this cheap in wall-clock paying goods-slot Renown would simply win every verse. Model-derived, NOT playtested — the run-3-to-run-6 sitting judges it, and the knob is this multiplier.
$spreadNote: Amounts also carry the generator's valueSpread (0.7) so this table and the generated Rites read the same way. A pure value split (spread 1) asks 5 copper ingots beside 400 nuts — true to the worth, but the two numbers say nothing to each other, and no player reads 'one ingot = eighty nuts' off a verse card. Softening towards each verse's own geometric-mean worth pulls the counts together (spreads here fall from 80-100x to 17-30x). It is value-NEUTRAL per verse by construction: what the dear slots gain, the cheap slots give up, so this knob never doubles as a difficulty lever. The cost is that a dear slot is no longer worth the same as a cheap one — expect the cheapest slots to be the popular answer, and watch whether choose-3-of-5 still poses a decision when the run-3-to-run-6 sitting happens.

generator.$comment: Run-2+ generator tuning (design §8: verseDemand(m) = baseQty · d^m, spotlight slots cheapest). demandGrowth is d; spotlight slots price at value × spotlightDiscount, off-spotlight at value × offSpotlightPremium. d is tuned against the fold's power ratio, not picked freely. A fold multiplies production by (1 + 0.02·Verdure) and Verdure is a square root of lifetime Renown, so that ratio starts near 3x across the first folds and settles at 1.10-1.15x from fold 7 on. d must sit just above the settled ratio: below it the gate stops gating, far above it the gate walls, because exponential demand always beats a power curve that is asymptotically linear. At the old 2.5 the twelfth fold asked ~1000x the wall-clock of the first; at 1.45 it asks ~2.5x, and folds 2-8 still run faster than the first (which is the prestige promise). spotlightDiscount / offSpotlightPremium are still first guesses.
generator.$valueSpreadNote: How hard a good's own worth divides its slot's value into a unit count: amount = target / (unit^spread x pivot^(1-spread)), pivot being the geometric mean worth of that verse's picks. 1 is the pure value split that produced '260 glow salve or 20000 berry preserves' — the same offering twice over, in two numbers that look nothing alike. 0.7 cuts that gap to about a fifth of what it was while keeping the dearest slot within ~4x the cheapest in value, which is the same order as the spotlight lever (0.6 / 1.5), so the choose-3-of-5 decision survives. Push it lower for legibility and the cheap slots simply win; 0.5 would make the dear slot cost ~9x the cheap one. Value-neutral per verse — see $spreadNote.
generator.$breadthNote: The fold gate grows in BREADTH, not depth. Every second migration a verse asks for one more filled slot (chooseCount + m/chooseCountPerMigrations, capped at chooseCountMax), and the generator adds a goods slot in step so the choice margin the authored Rite has (5 slots, choose 3) never narrows. Breadth costs stationing, kith slots and map coverage rather than wait-time, and it is BOUNDED by how many slots a verse has — so unlike a quantity multiplier it can never outrun the player's power curve. The per-verse clamp in Rite.RequiredSlots is the real guarantee: a verse always keeps at least one slot of choice even where a lean zone gives the generator too few candidates to widen.
generator.$specimenSlotNote: specimenSlotFraction PRICES the specimen slot instead of tabling it: its count is this fraction of the geometric mean of the same verse's goods asks, floored at the authored count, and skipped on zone order 1-2 whose hour-one pacing is pinned. Added 2026-08-12, replacing the per-zone table in $specimenRampNote as the live lever. That table rested on a premise the built game does not honour: design S8 priced the drawer as a lane that fills LINEARLY (posted familiars x time x chance) while goods compound, but Simulation.Deliver gives the WHOLE delivery its rolled tier, so a Choice roll credits the batch's full amount. The drawer is therefore total gathering x Choice chance — it rides the goods curve exactly, a percent or two behind it. Against that, ANY authored count decays into no ask at all: a save sitting on the river bend's verse at fold 2 held ~12K choice finds against an ask of 1. A fraction cannot decay, because both sides carry the same zone ramp and the same demandGrowth^m forever, and it cannot wall, because it asks for a slice of what the same run's gathering already produced. 0.4 puts the river bend's verse at ~1000 against that ~12K drawer (~8%) — a real ask that is still well under a goods slot, since the drawer pools EVERY resource's Choice rolls while a goods slot draws on one stock. This fraction is now the whole lever; raise it if the slot is still answered out of the drawer, lower it if the luck lane starts walling. Derived from ONE observed save, NOT playtested — the run-3-to-run-6 sitting judges it.
